meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone hear Owen first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And was Owen heard before it went in?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58; I'm writing those down. Plenty of people draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale. And you still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up, then. And whatever that screen shows, this stays off Owen's record and it stays quiet.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote Shakespeare every day of the week. A wrong line is a careless mistake, not proof of anything.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Seventeen-year-olds change their argument between outline and essay. Let me see both.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, the day before the zero. Put a seventeen-year-old on the spot with a teacher he thinks has it in for him and he freezes, Hale. What are you proposing?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class is not a weekend at home. You've shown me five things and still no answer: what are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.

Then leave it out of the room; under 4.3 the software establishes nothing on its own, and the company that sells it says the same. I'm not going to ask a third time, Hale. Put something on the table or I walk down to the principal.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Then he does it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and he does it privately, not in front of his class. I want 4.4 and that promise about his record in an email tonight. And it gets marked before December 1.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Tonight, in writing, and you still haven't told me it's marked before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, after school. Put that in tonight's email with the rest.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
And Thursday after school, marked well before December 1. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
No. Just the email tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday after school, marked before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement in writing, including the written promise that nothing goes on his file. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite Thursday after school with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and the mark in before December 1; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and offered to pull it up for her to check, which gave her something she could verify instead of an opinion.
What cost ground: you kept laying out evidence while she was asking what you were proposing, which made her sharper and pushed her toward threatening the principal.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay appearing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, came closer to that night than anything else you said; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she opens by asking whether Owen was heard first, tell her straight away that you spoke with him on November 2, rather than letting that question sit until your fourth piece of evidence.
